report.source_text: A 73-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with constitutional syndrome, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. She had a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, pancreatic cysts, and fibromyalgia, with no risk of exposure to pollutants.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old woman presented with constitutional syndrome, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Initial workup included a CT scan of the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis, which revealed peritoneal effusion with signs of peritoneal carcinomatosis, particularly in the lesser omentum, and edema of the adnexa. A subsequent biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of Malignant Peritoneal Mesothelioma (MPM) of the epidermoid type. The patient underwent cytoreductive surgery (resection of round and falciform ligament, and resection of omental cake/partial resection of the greater omentum) and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC). Due to the overall extension of the disease, she was referred for palliative chemotherapy, to which she has shown a partial response. Her history included pancreatic cysts (documented as serous), but no risk of exposure to pollutants.
